name: JOYCE, the Hon. Barnaby Thomas Gerard

headline.note: Private farm, nightclub, accounting and self-employment roles lack full-time evidence. Parliamentary testimony identifies QIDC banking employment, initially government-owned and later affected by Suncorp Metway restructuring; the banking interval needs a control-sensitive split. Reserve service is not assumed full-time. Ownership of the practice is distinguished from labour. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: Joyce's website gives study from 1986 to 1989; sources vary between Bachelor of Accounting, Financial Accounting and Bachelor of Financial Administration wording. Study load and employment overlap are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Unidentified farms in northern NSW and Queensland
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract supplies the role and years; biographical accounts place farm work around northern NSW and Queensland and also mention nightclub work without dates. Employers, exact dates, hours, remuneration, leave and continuity are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private farm employment is supported, but no substantive full-time interval is established.

career_spells.employer: Wicklow Hotel, Armidale (payroll entity unresolved); possible additional venue(s) unresolved
career_spells.evidence_note: SBS2018 identifies Wicklow Hotel, Armidale, and places bouncer work during university; SBS2022 broadly places such work after graduation. Venue identity is supported but chronology is not reconciled. Other publicly indexed interview material also names Wicklow. Exact dates, hours, remuneration, leave, legal employer and possible additional venues remain unresolved; no allocation to the whole study or1989–1991 farm interval.
career_spells.counting_note: Dates, substantive full-time status and/or leave remain insufficiently evidenced; no headline years calculated.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract gives accountant from1991 to1994. Joyce's website says three years at an unidentified chartered firm followed by a short American-multinational cost-accounting role. In a27November2024 House speech Joyce identifies that multinational as Conagra and describes himself as a cost accountant there. This resolves one employer but not the firm, internal transition, exact dates, legal payroll entity, hours or leave.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but employer boundaries and full-time status are not established.

career_spells.employer: Queensland Industry Development Corporation (QIDC); Suncorp Metway transition requires clarification
career_spells.evidence_note: Frozen 1994–1998 banking range retained. Joyce names QIDC in 2009 official testimony; his 2013 speech says five years as it moved toward Suncorp Metway. RBA confirms wholly state-owned QIDC before 1 December 1996 merger. The 1998 annual report describes partial sale, capital notes, trustee voting and limited state governance rights. Overall interval is not uniformly private or public: exact payroll transitions, substantive control dates, appointment/departure, hours and leave remain unresolved. Rounded five years does not justify a guessed start.
career_spells.counting_note: Government enterprise employment is identified, but a control-sensitive split of the banking interval and full-time status require further evidence; neither headline total calculated.

career_spells.employer: Barnaby Joyce & Co., St George, Queensland
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract gives self-employed accountant from 1998 to 2005. Narrative sources identify the firm and location but variously say it began in 1999 or operated for ten years. Legal registration, exact start/end, hours, leave, staff and whether work continued after Senate commencement are unresolved; the frozen range is retained. ABR identifies sole-trader entity ABN 48 726 796 727 and trading name from 16 December 1999; registration date is not substituted for official 1998 commencement. September 2005 ABC interview says brother Michael had taken over management while Barnaby retained an interest. No evidence that ownership meant continuing paid labour; official 2005 work end retained without inventing exact departure.
career_spells.counting_note: Private self-employment is supported, but conflicting boundaries and unknown hours prevent calculation.

career_spells.employer: Australian Army Reserve — Royal Queensland Regiment
career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary material, citing biographical sources, records Army Reserve service from 1996 to 2001. Paid-duty days, hours, rank, breaks and overlap with banking and accountancy work are unresolved; Reserve service is not assumed full-time.
career_spells.counting_note: Public military service is supported, but no substantive full-time interval or FTE is established.

career_spells.employer: National Party of Australia / Liberal National Party of Queensland
career_spells.role: Member, candidate, parliamentary representative and leader
career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary material records Nationals membership from 1995, Queensland LNP affiliation during Senate service, and resignation from the Nationals on 27 November 2025. Separate party remuneration and hours are unresolved; parliamentary offices are recorded within elected service.
career_spells.counting_note: Party activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster gives first federal service; secondary parliamentary chronology gives Senate service from 1 July 2005 until resignation on 8 August 2013.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Parliamentary chronology records House service from the 7 September 2013 election until the High Court held the 2016 election invalid on 27 October 2017. Ministerial and party-room offices are nested within this spell.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Joyce returned at the 2 December 2017 by-election and remains the frozen-roster Member for New England. Ministerial, shadow and party-room offices are nested within elected service. No employment is inferred for the parliamentary gap.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster identifies One Nation; secondary material records formal joining on 8 December 2025 after a short independent interval. Remuneration and hours are unresolved and parliamentary service is recorded separately.
career_spells.counting_note: Party activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: St Vincent de Paul Society (local conference/legal entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: 2011 local-government assembly speaker biography identifies longstanding membership; Joyce personally refers to work with the organisation in20October2020 House speech reproduced by OpenAustralia. Specific duties, branch, appointment/cessation and paid versus voluntary basis are not resolved. The earlier thesis claim of sixteen years and counselling is not adopted without the original interview. No employment is inferred merely from membership.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: 2013 ALGA institutional speaker biography identifies Acting Treasurer of Queensland Nationals concurrent with accountancy practice. Term boundaries, remuneration, weekly hours and exact overlap unreported; neither1998 practice start nor2004 election is adopted as a party-office boundary. Separate party organisational service from elected-office leadership and accountancy labour.
career_spells.counting_note: Party organisational work excluded from public/private headline; no paid full-time role inferred.

research_notes: The frozen official 1998–2005 self-employment range is retained despite narrative claims that Barnaby Joyce & Co. began in 1999 and operated for ten years.
Unnamed early employers remain unresolved rather than being guessed from industry descriptions.
Army Reserve service overlapped private employment and is not treated as full-time public employment.
House service is split around the 2017 High Court disqualification and by-election; no work is invented for the gap.

2026-10-01 follow-up: primary Senate testimony resolves QIDC identity; RBA history and 1998 employer report replace unsupported private-bank classification with unresolved mixed-control interval. No whole-period public total inferred from state ownership before merger.

Business-register identity and contemporaneous ABC brother interview resolve registration and ownership/management distinctions; separate nightclub role added without guessed dates. Searched chartered-firm/multinational names, bank/history reports and Reserve sources; no exact hours, early employer identities or service-duty records found. Member education page timed out; old ABC URL inaccessible, current ABC transcript recovered. Original 2013 Hansard link inaccessible; reproduction labelled. Continue with payroll/control records, original practice succession documents and specific employer identities.

Second follow-up2October2026 resolves Wicklow Hotel venue for previously unnamed bouncer employment, retaining unknown dates because reports differ on study overlap. Public GQ interview index independently mentions Wicklow; page redirected to cookie screen, no further access attempted.

Early accountancy-firm and American-multinational searches again yielded unnamed sequence, not employer identities/hours. A secondary blog quotes older Age Moree-nightclub account and SMH two-year Wicklow account; treat these as original-article leads, not proof of another employer or fixed two-year interval. UTas thesis mirror mentions sixteen years of St Vincent de Paul volunteering citing Fidler2006; original ABC21November2006 interview not retrieved, so charity detail remains a lead pending primary corroboration. Avoid repeating exhausted generic biography searches; next focus named venue archives, original interview and employer histories.

Follow-up3October2026 locates independent2011 assembly biography and first-person2020 House speech confirming St Vincent de Paul activity; adds a separate excluded nonprofit record without adopting unverified sixteen-year duration or counselling title. Original ABC21November2006 URL https://www.abc.net.au/local/stories/2006/11/21/1793869.htm returned404; linked archive returned Internal Error. The Age2005 original Moree-bouncer article returned non-retryable reader error; not accessed through a restriction-bypassing mirror. Search click invalid-arguments errors were recovered by reading public Wikipedia source-link HTML; local missing bs4 recovered using Python standard-library HTMLParser. Further volunteer terms, venue chronology and unnamed accountant employers remain unresolved.

Fourth follow-up4October2026 materially identifies Conagra as the previously unnamed American multinational: Joyce's first-person27November2024 House speech says he was a cost accountant there. The chartered accountancy firm, exact transition, payroll entity, hours and leave remain unresolved. Exact Wicklow and St Vincent de Paul searches repeated the two-year and sixteen-year secondary leads without primary term evidence; those durations were not adopted.

Follow-up2026-10-04: Targeted Conagra and chartered-firm identity queries surfaced a27June2013 Senate speech at https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2013-06-27.149.1 corroborating the already identified multinational, without employee dates or payroll entity. Archived2013 council speaker biographies repeat the unnamed firm/three-year sequence, not appointment evidence.9September2026 House speech https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2026-09-09.132.1 distinguishes Joyce’s Reserve service from his grandfather’s full-time military service; relative hours are not attributed to Joyce. Current staff job advertisements concern employees of his office, not his own accountant hours. No materially new employment fact; defer generic biographies and seek actual historical firm or bank personnel records.

Follow-up2026-10-05: Institutional2013 ALGA speaker biography identifies omitted Queensland Nationals Acting Treasurer office; added separately with unknown term/pay/hours and no practice-date substitution. Exact Conagra/chartered-firm and QIDC queries returned existing cost-accountant/unnamed firm narrative only. Indexed2012 original newspaper Conagra story corroborates known employer but not appointment/payroll; no paywall bypass or co-worker facts assigned. Wicklow part-time search found no hours. Corporate merger context remains distinct from personal payroll transition; next priority actual firm identification, bank personnel/control instrument and party office register.
open_questions: Which farms employed Joyce from 1989 to 1991, and what were the dates, hours and breaks, including any nightclub work?
What was the chartered accountancy firm, and what were the exact Conagra legal payroll entity, transition dates, hours and leave?
What paid-duty days, rank, hours and breaks applied to Army Reserve service?
Was there paid non-parliamentary work during the 27 October–2 December 2017 eligibility gap?
What were precise QIDC/Suncorp payroll and control transitions, working hours and leave within official 1994–1998 banking range, and how does the five-year narrative reconcile?
When did Michael take over practice management, when did Barnaby cease personal client work, and what hours/leave applied before and after Senate commencement? ABR dates alone cannot answer.
What were Wicklow Hotel employment dates, legal payroll entity and hours; was work during or after university, and were there separate Moree or other venues?
Which St Vincent de Paul conference, duties, dates and hours applied, and was this entirely voluntary? Original2006 interview remains unavailable; no sixteen-year interval inferred.
What were Queensland Nationals Acting Treasurer appointment/cessation, remuneration and hours, and what exact overlap applied to the accountancy practice?
